newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Nov 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Nov 19.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Goodyear Tyre & Rubber Company has returned to South Africa, buying 60 percent of Consol Ltd tyre company Contred from Anglovaal Industries for 568 million rand in a move touted as a vote of confidence in government's macroeconomic plan.
- Banks have borrowed foreign exchange to alleviate the cash crunch, making the money market shortage fall about one billion rand and fuelling bullish sentiment in the bond market.

- Industrial group Barlow exceeded forecasts for the year to September, lifting share earnings, excluding exceptional items, 27 percent to 329.2 cents, after a strong contribution from its offshore operations.

- Times Media Ltd's attributable profit dipped 15 percent to 35.7 million rand in the six months to September, but a 47 percent surge in contributions from core publications, including Business Day, boosted operating profit 25 percent to 47.8 million rand.
- Two power blocks have emerged in the race for Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd's 47 percent stake in JCI Ltd, with a repositioning of the main contenders.
- The failure of seven transport unions and road freight employers to resolve a transport industry wage dispute Monday night could see the delivery of cash and goods grind to a halt tomorrow.
- Senior National Party leaders, including Roelf Meyer and Hernus Kriel, came in for a withering criticism from the truth commission at its second Bisho masscare hearing on Monday.

- Consol Ltd, the packaging group, is selling Contred, its tyre manufacturing subsidiary, to Goodyear Tire & Rubbe, the international rubber products group, and Anglovaal Industries, Consol's parent company, for an effective 1.07 billion rand, the three companies said on Monday.
- Barlow, the industrial group, exceeded forecasts by lifting headline earnings in the year to September 30 by 27 percent to 329.2 cents a share.
- Unionists were confident on Monday that Wednesday's planned national trucking industry strike, which they saids would disrupt all sectors of the economy, could be sustained for at least two weeks.

- Adcock Ingram, the pharmaceutical group which recently merged with Premier Pharmaceutical has reported earnings for the yera to September 30 of 98.2 cents a share, a 3.4 percent increase on the previous year's 95 cents a share.
- Rescue teams on Monday night freed 15 miners who were trapped in two mines at Western Deep Levels' East gold mine near Carltonville after a rockfall claimed at least one life.

- Crime in Johannesburg is declining, due largely to the influx of policemen from other provinces for Operation Urban Strike -- but Egoli residents' good fortune had left a bitter taste in the mounts of their neighbours north of the Juskei River.
